narrative: My daughter was three years old. She began breathing very quickly and shallowly, and the spaces between her ribs sucked in with every breath. She was hot to the touch the whole time. She did not have a rash, her bowels were normal, and her neck moved freely.
My son was ten months old. He could not feed and became weak and sleepy. His lips had a bluish tinge. He had no rash, no loose stools, and he did not vomit much.

My daughter was four years old. Over about a week she had repeated bouts of fever with chills and then sweating. She had no cough, no rash, and her neck was not stiff. She died at home before we could get her treatment.

My son was about eighteen months old. He lived with us in a malarious area. He had two convulsions and then would not wake. His fast breathing and unconsciousness continued until he died on the second day.

My son was three years old. A few days after we returned he developed high fever with shaking chills. He vomited and complained of headache, and soon his eyes and skin looked yellow. He passed very little urine and what came was very dark.

My son was two years old. He suddenly began passing large amounts of watery stool over and over, and he vomited several times. Within a single day he became very weak and his eyes sank into his face. He became drowsy and unresponsive and died the same day.

My daughter was about fourteen months old. She had loose, frequent stools for several days, sometimes with a little mucus, along with a mild fever and vomiting. She became very thirsty and then refused to drink. She had no cough and no rash on her body.

My son was one year old. Over those days he steadily lost weight and dried out. His eyes became deeply sunken, his mouth stayed dry, and he hardly passed any urine. He was too weak to cry properly and made no tears.

My baby was born too early, after about seven months of pregnancy. He was very small and thin and weighed very little, and his skin was reddish and looked thin and transparent. From the moment he was born he had trouble breathing, his chest pulled in and he breathed fast and grunted. He was too weak to suckle and we had to give drops of milk.

My daughter was born about two months before she was due. She was tiny and her skin was thin and red. She had no fever and no rash. She had spells where her breathing stopped for a while, and she died on the fifth day of life.
I gave birth to twins early, and this was the smaller one. She could not keep warm and her hands and feet were always cold. She had no strength to feed. There was no rash and she never had a fever.

My baby came early because I had heavy bleeding in pregnancy. He was very small and immediately had difficulty breathing, working hard with grunting and indrawing of the chest. He had no fever and no rash and his cord was clean.
My son was born when I was about eight months pregnant. He was small and light with a weak, thin cry. He fed poorly and tired quickly at the breast. He weakened steadily and died on the fourth day.

My baby was born at full term but the labour was very long and difficult and lasted more than a day at home before we reached the clinic. The birth attendant rubbed her and she eventually gasped, but she never became active or fed well. She did not have a fever and there was no rash. She never suckled properly and her breathing was irregular.

My labour was obstructed and went on for a very long time. The midwife worked on him until he started to gasp. After that he never woke up properly, did not cry normally, and could not suck. He had no fever and no rash.

When my daughter was born the cord was wrapped tightly around her neck. Once she finally breathed she remained weak with poor muscle tone and would not feed. She had no fever and no rash, and her cord stump was clean.
I delivered at home and the baby was stuck for a long time during the birth. He came out limp and pale and did not cry, only gasping weakly. He had no fever and there was no rash.

My baby came feet first and the delivery was very difficult and slow. She remained weak and unresponsive, never opened her eyes properly, and could not feed. Her breathing stayed irregular and she did not improve, and she died early in the first days of life.

My daughter was two years old and had not received her childhood vaccinations. She first had a high fever, red watery eyes, a runny nose and a harsh cough for a few days. After the rash she became more ill, her breathing became fast and difficult, and she had loose stools. She grew weaker and died about ten days after the fever began.
My son was three years old and never got his vaccines. He started with fever, red sore eyes and a cough. He became very dehydrated and weak. He died about a week and a half after the illness began.

My daughter was about eighteen months old. There was a rash illness going around our community at the time. She developed a high fever with red watery eyes and a barking cough, and then a red rash spread over her body starting from the face. She stopped feeding and became drowsy.
My son was four years old and unvaccinated. He had no stiff neck at first but his mind was clearly affected. He never recovered his senses and died a few days after the seizures began.

My daughter was two years old and had missed her vaccines. She had a fever, runny nose, cough and red eyes, then a red rash appeared on her face and spread down. She wasted away and died some weeks after the rash.

My son was one year old. He became ill quickly with a very high fever and a lot of crying, and he refused to feed. He vomited several times. He slipped into unconsciousness and died within two days of becoming sick.

My daughter was three years old. She suddenly developed a very high fever and a severe headache, and she vomited again and again. She quickly became drowsy and confused, then had a convulsion and lost consciousness. She had no cough and her breathing was not fast at first.

My son was eight months old. He became feverish and gave a strange high-pitched cry that was different from his normal crying. The soft spot on top of his head was tense and bulging, and he did not want to be moved or have light near him. He grew very drowsy and floppy, and then his body began to jerk in convulsions.
My daughter was two years old. She had a fever and then began behaving strangely, not recognising us and saying confused things. Her neck felt stiff when we tried to move her head.

My son was four years old. His neck became stiff and painful and he could not stand the light, keeping his eyes covered. Within a day he had a convulsion and became unconscious. He had no cough, no rash, and his bowels were normal.

My daughter was about two years old. She had a poor appetite, was often unhappy and listless, and had episodes of diarrhoea. We did not have enough food at home and she ate very little. She became very weak and died slowly at home.

My son was about eighteen months old. I had stopped breastfeeding early and there was little food for him. Over time he became extremely thin, with loose folds of skin, a wasted face and visible ribs and joints. He was not feverish most of the time and had no rash.

My daughter was three years old. Her face, hands and legs became swollen and puffy, and her belly was large, though the rest of her looked wasted. She had no appetite and was apathetic, barely reacting to anything. She weakened over weeks and died.

My son was two years old. He had failed to grow for many months while other children his age thrived. He became severely wasted, with thin limbs and a shrunken face, and you could count his ribs. He had no rash and was not usually feverish.

My daughter was about fifteen months old. She was weak and had no appetite, and later her legs and feet became swollen and puffy. Her hair was sparse and pale and her skin was dry and flaky. We were very poor and could not feed her properly.

My baby was born at home at the normal time and seemed well at first. Her skin looked yellow and a little mottled, and the stump of the cord looked red and smelled bad. She became floppy and difficult to wake, and her cry became weak. She did not have a rash.
My son was born at home and was healthy for the first days. On the third day he became dull and stopped feeding well. He felt hot and his skin turned yellow. The cord area looked a little red.

My waters broke a long time before my daughter was born. Her skin looked mottled and her hands and feet were cold. Later she had some jerking movements. She would not wake to feed and her cry faded, and she died within the first week of life.

My son seemed fine when he was born but on about the sixth day he became irritable and then very lethargic. He vomited his feeds and his belly looked swollen. His temperature was unstable, sometimes hot and sometimes too cold, and his hands and feet were cold.
My daughter was delivered in unclean conditions and her cord was cut with a dirty blade. She had no rash elsewhere. She became unresponsive and died on the seventh day of life.

My son looked different from birth and the midwife said his heart did not form properly. He breathed fast and never gained weight well, staying small and weak. He did not have a fever and there was no rash or diarrhoea. He became more blue and breathless over time and died at a few months of age.

My daughter was born with an open swelling on her lower back that was covered only by a thin membrane and leaked fluid. She had no rash elsewhere. She became increasingly unwell from the infections and died in early infancy.

My son was born with his lip and the roof of his mouth split open. He caught chest infections again and again from the milk going the wrong way. He grew weaker with each illness and died in his first months of life.

My daughter's head was unusually large at birth and grew bigger and bigger over the following weeks while the rest of her stayed small. The soft spot was wide and tense and her eyes seemed pushed downward. She had no fever or rash.

My son was born with something wrong with his heart, the clinic said, and from birth he was often breathless and turned bluish, especially when feeding or crying. He could only feed a little at a time before tiring and sweating, and he hardly grew. He had no rash and no diarrhoea.

My son was two years old. Then he developed a high fever and quickly became very ill, much sicker than an ordinary fever. He breathed fast, his hands and feet turned cold and mottled even though his body was hot, and he passed very little urine. He became drowsy and unresponsive and his colour was grey.
My daughter was three years old. She had no stiff neck and no real cough. She grew confused and then unresponsive, her pulse fast and weak, and she died quickly over about a day.
My son was about eighteen months old. He developed a fever and refused his feeds, and within a day he became floppy and very ill. He hardly passed any urine.

My daughter was four years old. Her hands and feet were cold and her skin was mottled, while her body burned hot. Her breathing and heartbeat were very fast and she passed little urine. She slipped into unconsciousness and died.
My son was one year old. He stopped feeding and became very drowsy. He passed almost no urine. He had no cough, no rash and no stiff neck.

My daughter was about eighteen months old. From early in her life she failed to grow and was always sick. She had white patches in her mouth that would not go away, long-lasting diarrhoea, and one chest infection after another. The glands in her neck and groin were swollen, and she had a constant skin rash.
My son was two years old. For most of his life he was a sickly child who never thrived. He had a cough that lasted for months and steadily lost weight. His mother had died of a long illness.

My son was about one year old, born to a mother who was chronically ill. His belly was swollen with an enlarged liver and spleen, and the glands around his body were swollen. He had stopped reaching the milestones he had earlier achieved and was wasting.

My daughter was three years old and had been in poor health since she was a baby. She was severely thin and wasted, had episodes of fever that came and went for weeks, and suffered persistent skin rashes and sores. Neither she nor her mother had been tested or treated for any chronic infection.
My baby was breastfed by me, and I had been sick for years without treatment. He never grew properly and was always ill. His weight kept falling and his glands were swollen.

My son was four years old. His grandfather, who lived with us, had a long cough for many months. He slowly lost weight and his appetite faded. There was no sudden high fever or fast breathing at first.

My daughter was three years old. She had a persistent cough lasting many weeks and recurring low fevers, with sweating at night. She declined slowly over months rather than suddenly, and she eventually died.
My son was about two years old. He had a mild fever on and off and sweated at night. There was a person with a long-standing cough in our household.
My daughter was four years old. She ran low fevers, especially in the evening, and had drenching night sweats. She became too weak to walk and died.

My son was three years old. Over several months he had a long cough, gradually lost weight and energy, and stopped growing. A member of our household had had a chronic cough and weight loss for a long time. His illness was slow and drawn out rather than a sudden fever.
My son was three years old. We pulled him out and tried to revive him, pressing on his chest and turning him over to let water out, but he never breathed again. He died right there by the water.
My daughter was about two years old. She reached up and pulled a pot of boiling water from the fire onto herself. She was in terrible pain and the burns were extensive.

My son was four years old. He was crossing the road near the market when a motorbike struck him at speed. He was thrown and hit his head hard on the ground, and he lost consciousness immediately. He died on the way to the hospital.

My son was about eighteen months old. He climbed and then fell from a high platform in our compound, landing on his head. He had been a completely healthy child before the fall, with no fever, cough or illness of any kind.

My daughter was about one year old. I left her for a short while near a large bucket of water that I had filled for washing. She had been a healthy, lively baby that day with no illness, fever or breathing trouble beforehand.

My son was four years old. Then he suddenly became restless, frightened and irritable. He could not drink, even though he was thirsty, because his throat would go into painful spasms and he panicked at the sight of water.

My daughter was three years old. Weeks before, she had been bitten by a neighbour's dog that later disappeared. Whenever we offered her water she would jerk and choke and become terrified, so she refused to drink at all. She had convulsive spasms and then grew limp, and she died within a few days.

My son was four years old. He had been scratched and bitten by a dog that died soon afterwards, but his wound healed and he received no injections. About a month later he developed a fever and then began acting oddly, very restless and easily startled.

My daughter was about four years old. Then she suddenly could not swallow and would choke and panic when she tried to drink, so she avoided all water. She drooled constantly and could not manage her own saliva.

My son was four years old and had been bitten on the hand by a dog more than three weeks before, but we did not get him any vaccine. He first complained of tingling and odd sensations at the old bite site.
My son was three years old. Other relatives had the same blood condition. He collapsed from the severe anaemia and died.

My daughter was about two years old. Since infancy she had been anaemic and her eyes were often yellow, and she had needed blood transfusions more than once. She had this inherited blood condition that ran in our family, and during this sudden severe episode she collapsed and died.

My son was about eighteen months old. He caught infections often. During his final illness he developed a fever and then became severely pale and listless very quickly, breathing fast with a racing heart.

My daughter was four years old. She had lifelong anaemia with pale, yellow-tinged eyes and recurring crises of severe bone and joint pain. Despite reaching the clinic she could not be saved and died during this severe episode.
My son was three years old. He had repeated painful crises over the years and was known to carry the family blood disorder. The anaemia overwhelmed him and he died at home.
